generated: Generated for the px + greenery + harmony drop. Regenerate rather than hand-edit: the art half is read from TerrainPx.json, the gameplay half is the declared table below.
derivedFromNote: Three hashes because three files own the result: pxKit + pxKit2 own the marks, pixelLanguage owns the key vector and the band ramps. Station/rowhouse precedent — stamp all the owners, never one.

light.note: fixed upper-left key + back rim, view space, as TreeRig3.LIGHT; PxLang.setKey flips every bake

channels.albedo: pre-lit at the fixed key, one band up/down at most
channels._unlit: the authored bands, no directional light
channels._mask: R key N·L · G rim · B height NORMALISED PER TILE · A coverage
channels._normal: R x · G y-up · B out
channels._blend: R coverage order 1–255 · G height on blend.hKit (comparable between materials) · B mark id hash, 0 = matrix · A 255

valueLadder: sand › foreshore › path › marram › shelf › ledge › ripple › oysterreef › dirt › rockweed › marsh › sedge › eelgrass › silt › grass › shingle › talus › mud › bank › musselbed › irishmoss

traverse_legend.mode: walk = ordinary floor · wade = normally under water, entered at a wading cost · face = a vertical/steep face material, never on the terrain mesh
traverse_legend.speed_mul: multiplier on base walk speed. grass = 1.00 is the reference; path is the only material above it.
traverse_legend.footstep: sound class: turf earth gravel sand wet_sand mud cobble rubble rock blades peat marsh weed shell
traverse_legend.grip: 0–1, used for slide/slip rolls. rockweed 0.18 is the floor of the kit and irishmoss is next; path 0.92 is the ceiling.
traverse_legend.vehicle: cart / ATV passable. Foreshore is true because hard wet sand is a road; dry sand is not.
traverse_legend.hazard: slip (footing goes out) · cut (shell edges) · sinking (silt) · bog (mud) · turn_ankle (rolling stone) · fall (the lip above a bank)

blend.why: Most of this terrain is painted, not tiled by hand, so every material has to survive arriving at partial weight. The failure mode is not subtle: cross-fading two banded palettes produces colour that is in neither of them, which is what pass two did and what the authored edge strips were built to replace. A paint tool must CHOOSE a material per texel and never average two of them.
blend.choose:
For each material k painted at this texel, with weight w_k in 0..1:
  order_k  = _blend.R                                         (1..255)
  height_k = hKit[0] + _blend.G/255 * (hKit[1] - hKit[0])     (texels)
  score_k  = w_k * 255 - order_k + heightGain * (height_k + bias_k)
Take the material with the highest score and use its albedo unchanged. No mixing, no alpha.
w_k * 255 >= order_k alone is the plain coverage test; the height term is what lets a stone keep its whole silhouette against sand instead of being nibbled at the frontier.
blend.whyOrder: Every texel of one authored mark carries the SAME order value, so a cobble, a tussock or a puddle arrives whole. The order is laid out along one wrapping noise field, so a half-weight patch is a blotch with a wandering frontier rather than a dither screen. markLead says which arrives first as the weight rises: 1 = the marks (a few cobbles land on the sand long before the grit does, which is how a shingle beach actually encroaches), 0 = the matrix (silt closes over the flat as a surface and its burrows come last).

frontier.note: Two rules recover the authored edge language per texel, so a painted boundary looks like a baked strip. Sample the winner at the four neighbours; let A be this texel's winner and B a neighbour's.
frontier.cutAndShade: If A stands proud of B (height_A + bias_A > height_B + bias_B) and B is this texel, multiply B's albedo by shadeMul for shadeTexels texels on A's SOUTH and EAST sides — that is A's cut face throwing its shade downlight. Materials whose fringe is "lip" (ledge, shelf) throw lipTexels instead.
frontier.litRim: On A's NORTH and WEST sides, multiply A's albedo by litRimMul on about half the frontier texels (hash the texel) — the broken lit rim where the higher material's edge faces the key.
frontier.fringe: The strips in Edges/ still carry the authored fringe (blades, crumbs, spilled stones) and are still the right thing along a boundary the level actually cares about. The frontier rules above are what a painted boundary gets for free.

blend.variants: Where a material ships _v2/_v3, pick per tile at random so a painted field does not repeat every 8 m.

edges.contract: A over B along a wandering line. A's side is opaque for its first 6 px — lay the strip so those rows sit inside the A tile and the engine's hard boundary falls under them. B's side is alpha except the marks. N = A above · S = A below · W = A left · E = A right; outer o<Q> = A fills quadrant Q, inner i<Q> = B fills it. Every orientation is baked with the key upper-left, so never rotate a strip.
edges.painted: A boundary the paint tool made does not need a strip — see TerrainPx.json blend.frontier. Use a strip where a level cares about the line.
edges.note: A strip is art, not collision: the traverse row of the material a texel resolves to is what gameplay reads, and the paint tool resolves every texel to exactly one material (blend.choose).

_excluded.sandstone: The face material (Art/pxTerrainRig.js, still a 2 px texel) and everything in Art/Tilesets/CliffPx are out of this drop by request. Bank is the only face material included, and it is marked mode:face — it is here because it is baked in TerrainPx, not because a body walks on it.
_excluded.rock_px: Art/Sprites/Shore/RockPx (the pass-three iso rock kit) is out of this drop by request. Art/Sprites/Scatter/Rocks.png — the pixel kit own boulder sheet from pass three — IS included; it is part of this kit, delete it if the exclusion was meant to cover it too.
_excluded.walkable_masks: No per-scene walkable mask: not requested. A mask is derivable from the painted material id per texel plus the traverse rows here.

_confirm.declared: Every number under traverse is DECLARED, not measured — no rig carries footstep, grip or speed. They are ordered against each other so the set is internally consistent (path > grass > foreshore > sand > shingle > mud > silt; rockweed the slipperiest thing on the coast). Tune them as gameplay constants; the ordering is the art-side claim, the absolute values are not.
_confirm.wet_tide: tide_state names where a material normally sits, not a live wetness. A material below high water is dry at low tide and the shader knows it; grip does not currently move with the tide, and it probably should for ledge and shelf.
_confirm.vehicle: foreshore and path are the only surfaces a loaded cart crosses well. Marram is false to make trampling a cost; that is a design position, not a physical fact.
_confirm.hazard_cut: musselbed and oysterreef carry cut, which assumes a barefoot/soft-boot model. If footwear is not modelled, drop the flag rather than pricing it in speed.
